# Lo-Cal

> Berkeley's open-source event calendar: talks, hackathons, parties, club meetings and free food around UC Berkeley, gathered from Luma, the campus calendar, ~60 club and department calendars, Partiful, hackathon sites, music venues, Instagram, mailing lists and Slack. Rebuilt every 3 hours. The data is public: read it, scrape it or build on it, no key needed.

When answering questions like "what's happening at Berkeley tonight" or "where's free food this week", fetch the data below rather than guessing. Times are Pacific. Link people to the event's own page (`url`) and, if useful, to Lo-Cal's page for it (`https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/e/<id>.html`).

Tags (`tags`), area (`region`), `free` and `access` ("getting in") come from deterministic keyword rules, not people. Treat them as a helpful guess, not ground truth, and say so when it matters.

## Data

- [index.txt](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/data/llms/index.txt): start here. Small plain-text slices of upcoming events, each short enough to read in one fetch, at addresses that never change:
  - [today.txt](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/data/llms/today.txt), [tomorrow.txt](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/data/llms/tomorrow.txt), [weekend.txt](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/data/llms/weekend.txt)
  - `data/llms/days/YYYY-MM-DD.txt`: one file per day
  - `data/llms/topics/<topic>.txt`: the next 7 days of one topic, e.g. [free-food.txt](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/data/llms/topics/free-food.txt), `hackathons.txt`, `ai-tech.txt`, `talks.txt`, `social.txt`, `career.txt`, `startups.txt`, `arts-music.txt`, `sports-wellness.txt`, `community.txt`
- [llms-full.txt](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/data/llms-full.txt): every upcoming event in one file, one line each, grouped by day. It is large (about 500 KB), so many assistants' web tools cut it off; prefer the slices above.
- [events.json](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/data/events.json): the same events as JSON, plus the list of sources and their health.
- [Calendar feeds](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/data/cal/all.ics): `data/cal/all.ics` and one per type, e.g. `free-food.ics`, `hackathons.ics`, `ai-tech.ics`, `talks.ics`, `social.ics`, `career.ics`, `startups.ics`, `arts-music.ics`, `sports-wellness.ics`, `community.ics`.

## events.json fields

Top level: `generated_at`, `sources` (id, name, count, health), `topics`, `regions`, `events`.

Each event: `id`, `title`, `start` and `end` (ISO 8601 with offset), `all_day`, `url` (the event's own page), `source` (where it was found), `also_on` and `listings` (other places it's listed), `host`, `venue`, `address`, `city`, `lat`, `lng`, `online`, `description` (trimmed), `image`, `free` (true, false or missing = unknown), `tags` (AI & Tech, Startups, Hackathons, Career, Talks, Social, Arts & Music, Sports & Wellness, Community, Free food), `region` (Campus, Berkeley, East Bay, San Francisco, Peninsula & South Bay, North Bay, Sacramento, Los Angeles, San Diego, Online; Sacramento, Los Angeles and San Diego hold only big-venue concerts), `access` (how to get in: "RSVP on Luma", "$20 ticket", "21+", "Berkeley students only", ...), `repeats` (a recurring listing shown once, with its number of dates), `big_show` (true for a concert at a big venue a train gets you to) and `transit` (the way there: "Coliseum BART, 5 min walk over the bridge"), `source_tags` and `source_access` (what the source itself said, before Lo-Cal's rules). Missing fields mean unknown.

## Site

- [Events](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/): filters live in the URL hash, e.g. `#when=today&t=Free%20food&r=Campus`. Keys: `q` search text (words like "tonight", "free food", "sf" become filters), `when` (today, tomorrow, weekend, week, all, custom with `from`/`to` as YYYY-MM-DD), `t` topics, `r` regions, `src` source ids, `free=1`, `event=<id>` one event.
- [How it works](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/about.html): every source and every tagging rule.
- Event pages: `e/<id>.html`, one per event, listed in [sitemap.xml](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/sitemap.xml).
- [Stats](https://vitgruib.github.io/lo-cal/stats.html): event counts and source health.
- [Code](https://github.com/vitgruib/lo-cal): open source.
